comparison: Both evaluate the core TIP-eQTL identification (C42-C45, C30). OpenEval finds the results SUPPORTED with clear statistical thresholds and visual evidence. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, with all reviewers acknowledging the identification as a core finding and the evidence as 'convincing.'

Both address claims about TIPs explaining additional variance beyond SNPs (C47-C48, C155-C156). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, noting the ten-fold difference in numbers and cautioning about linkage versus causality, though acknowledging authors are careful in their claims.

Both evaluate effect directionality and causal inference (C49-C54). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED but notes causality remains 'somewhat speculative.' Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, emphasizing that 'linkage is just that, not definitive evidence' and noting insertion bias as an alternative explanation.

Both address upstream enrichment and causality inference (C55-C58, C158). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED though acknowledges linkage disequilibrium cannot be ruled out. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, noting insertion bias as an alternative and emphasizing the distinction between correlation and causation.

Both evaluate the relationship between TIP frequency and effect size (C59-C62). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with clear visual evidence and theoretical backing. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging it as part of the systematic case building for selection.

Both address condition-specificity of TIP-eQTLs (C63-C67). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with specific overlap percentages. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, with no challenges to the environmental comparison findings.

Both evaluate subspecies-specificity (C75-C79) and frequency patterns (C85-C88). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, noting the contrast with condition overlap. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 noting the finding about ancestral presence and differential retention as 'interesting.'

Both address TIP presence in wild ancestors (C80-C81, C91-C92, C162). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with data evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly SUPPORT this, with Reviewer 2 stating it 'may strengthen the argument' about selection on standing variation.

Both evaluate PBS selection analysis (C95-C99). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging that eQTL-TIPs show 'much stronger evidence for selection' and the combination of evidence is 'convincing.'

Both address the EG2 locus case study (C102-C110). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as a well-characterized example. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging the detailed examples as part of the systematic evidence.

Both evaluate EG2 haplotype frequency and selection analysis (C111-C121). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED though notes phenotypic link is correlative. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED as part of the convincing case examples.

Both address the OsGAP locus characterization (C122-C129). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with clear documentation. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, accepting it as one of the detailed gene examples.

Both evaluate OsGAP functional and selection analysis (C130-C137). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED though notes dormancy relevance is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED as part of the accepted case studies.

Both address the OsMPH1 case (C139-C148). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with strong selection evidence and parallel to SD1. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging the examples and the biological context they provide.

Both evaluate the overarching conclusion about TEs as major drivers (C2-C5, C169-C170, C31, C97, C99, C167-C168). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by comprehensive evidence. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 concerned about 'sweeping claims' given only 30 genes with strong selection evidence, and Reviewer 3 noting the study 'stops short of identifying causations.'

Both address the synthesis of evidence for TIP causality (C157-C158, C13, C53). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by multiple lines of evidence but acknowledges it remains an inference. Peer reviewers find this UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating that 'linkage is just that, not definitive evidence' and that transgenic experiments would be needed for convincing proof.

OpenEval evaluates TIP detection methodology and validation (C34-C41) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on the technical validation of TIP detection methods.

OpenEval evaluates frequency patterns contrasting eQTL-TIPs versus non-eQTL TIPs (C85-C90) as SUPPORTED, noting differential retention patterns. While peer R7 addresses some overlapping claims, this specific contrast and its implications for selection are not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates TIP presence in wild ancestors with frequency differences (C91-C94) as SUPPORTED but notes the explanation is speculative. While peer R8 addresses overlapping claims C91-C92, the specific frequency change analysis and drift versus selection discussion are not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates TIP multiplicity at genes (C159-C161) as SUPPORTED, noting enrichment at highly selected genes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on this clustering pattern.

OpenEval synthesizes findings about TIP age and selection (C162-C168) as SUPPORTED. While peer R8 and R13 address some overlapping claims, this specific synthesis combining age, standing variation, and phenotypic connections is not explicitly evaluated as a unit by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates study design and data sources (C28-C29, C32-C33) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on the methodological foundation.

OpenEval evaluates drought-related TIP-eQTL examples (C68-C74) as SUPPORTED with citation backing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on these stress-response examples.

OpenEval evaluates candidate gene identification from PBS analysis (C100-C101) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on this candidate gene framework.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims (C1, C6-C27) as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not evaluate the accuracy of background literature summaries.

OpenEval evaluates high-level summary claims (C30-C31) as SUPPORTED but redundant with detailed results. While peer R1 and R13 address overlapping claims, they evaluate the substantive findings rather than these summary statements specifically.

OpenEval evaluates contextual citations to prior work (C149-C154) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not evaluate the appropriateness of these contextual citations.
